about: Canvas rendering, input and eraser work (docs/perf/README.md). Counts are budgets enforced by apps/ios/Tests/VellumCoreTests/CanvasRenderingBudgetTests.swift. Times are main-thread busy time per frame from the benchmark on the iPhone Duo simulator in CI, compared by apps/ios/Scripts/perf-compare.py: Release times after scaling by the measured probe, Release p50 warning at 25% worse and Release p95 at 40%; Debug p50, unscaled, warning at 25%; the rest only record.

entries.measured: perf/canvas-rendering 2026-11-01 forge Linux Swift 6.4.2 (deterministic)
entries.note: A pan, and a pinch to the next level, after the view was drawn once, through InkTileBook and the path cache as the renderer uses them. Main built a path for every visible stroke on every redraw.

entries.measured: perf/canvas-rendering 2026-11-01 forge Linux Swift 6.4.2 (deterministic)
entries.note: A 60 x 30 pt stroke in the middle of the screen at zoom to everything: the screen area of the tiles InkTileBook asks the renderer to draw for it, 4 tiles (the tile anchor sits at the screen centre, the worst case). Main redrew the whole 951 x 669 view, background and grid included.

entries.measured: perf/canvas-rendering 2026-10-31 forge Linux Swift 6.4.2 (deterministic)
entries.note: Culling a view at 4x the zoom of everything. Main compared every stroke.

entries.measured: perf/canvas-rendering 2026-10-31 forge Linux Swift 6.4.2 (deterministic)
entries.note: Bounds are cached in the index. Main recomputed every stroke's bounds from its points on every redraw.

entries.measured: perf/canvas-rendering 2026-10-31 forge Linux Swift 6.4.2 (deterministic)
entries.note: Mean over the benchmark's 479-sample sweep at everything, tolerance 8 pt. Main recomputed every stroke's bounds and measured every segment of strokes near the tip.

entries.measured: perf/canvas-rendering 2026-10-31 forge Linux Swift 6.4.2 (deterministic)
entries.note: Mean over the same sweep.

entries.measured: perf/canvas-rendering 2026-10-31 forge Linux Swift 6.4.2 (deterministic)
entries.note: Most points turned into path on one Pencil move over a 10,000-sample stroke, two samples and two predictions a move. Main rebuilt the whole stroke every move.

entries.measured: perf/canvas-rendering 2026-11-01 forge Linux Swift 6.4.2 (deterministic)
entries.note: Erasing a stroke that spans the whole made-up plant while zoomed all the way in (1,000 pt/in): tile positions or cached tiles looked at to find the tiles it touched, counted by InkTileBook. The before is what #23 first did, every tile position in the stroke's bounds; main had no tiles.

entries.measured: feat/draw-with-finger 2026-11-01 (deterministic; checked by CI VellumCore tests)
entries.note: Draw with finger (#24): a finger stroke drawn live for 30 ms, then a second finger 60 ms after touchdown, inside FingerStrokeGate.secondFingerWindow (130 ms), through the canvas view's finger path on an InkSession. Strokes added to the ink and undo steps made. New with #24.

entries.measured: feat/draw-with-finger 2026-11-01 (deterministic; checked by CI VellumCore tests)
entries.note: The same cancelled finger stroke: bytes of ink-log records (framed) handed to the canvas saver. New with #24.

entries.measured: feat/draw-with-finger 2026-11-01 (deterministic; checked by CI VellumCore tests)
entries.note: A finger eraser sweep over three strokes cancelled by a second finger 80 ms after touchdown: strokes erased. The sweep holds its samples while pending, so nothing is erased. New with #24.

entries.measured: feat/snap-lasso-text 431a6a5 2026-11-02 CI run 41375765893 (deterministic; also Linux Swift)
entries.note: A lasso loop round the middle of the 10,000-stroke canvas, a quarter of its height across, at everything (#7): strokes whose cached bounds the index compared. The before is a plain scan of every stroke. New with #7.

entries.measured: feat/snap-lasso-text 431a6a5 2026-11-02 CI run 41375765893 (deterministic; also Linux Swift)
entries.note: The same lasso: points tested against the loop, Lasso.pointsTested (32) per stroke whose bounds meet the loop's (along its length for a stroke with fewer points). The before is every point of every stroke. New with #7.

entries.measured: feat/snap-lasso-text 2026-11-02 CI run 41364633767 (deterministic; also Linux Swift)
entries.note: Recognising a 10,000-sample circle when the Pencil holds still (#7): evenly spaced points tested against the candidate shapes, 63 points at 90 angles for the smallest bounding rectangle and 63 for the fit, the same however long the stroke. Runs once per hold, never per Pencil sample. The before is the stroke's samples, for scale. New with #7.

entries.measured: feat/snap-lasso-text 2026-11-02 CI run 41364633767 (deterministic; also Linux Swift)
entries.note: The same hold: the stroke's points read, twice (its length and bounds, then spacing 64 points along it). Once per hold. New with #7.

entries.measured: feat/measure-frame 2ac6670 2026-11-02 CI run 41399368174 (deterministic; checked by CI VellumCore tests)
entries.note: A measure or dimension tap (#8) snapping to the nearest ink end, corner or circle centre within 20 screen points: strokes whose cached bounds the index compares, the worst of ten taps across the middle of the made-up 10,000-stroke canvas at the zoom that fits it all. Through InkIndex, never the whole canvas (before: every stroke). New with #8.

entries.measured: feat/drawing-tools f3068dd 2026-11-04 CI run 41876112104 (deterministic; checked by CI VellumCore tests)
entries.note: A snap lookup on a crowded canvas (#40): pairs of segments or round strokes tested for crossing, the worst of ten lookups with a point to work from, in a made-up thicket of 400 hand-drawn strokes of 80 points all crossing, zoomed out to 0.25 points per inch. Crossings are looked for only among segments within reach of the tip and no further than the best point so far, swept along x, at most 128 of them, so never more than 8,128 pairs. Before: every segment on that canvas against every other.

entries.measured: feat/drawing-tools f3068dd 2026-11-04 CI run 41876112104 (deterministic; checked by CI VellumCore tests)
entries.note: The same lookups: points read from the strokes near the tip, each such stroke's points once. Nearly every stroke in this thicket runs through the place, which is what makes it the worst case: the index can rule out only what isn't near. Before: every point on that canvas.

entries.measured: feat/measure-frame 2ac6670 2026-11-02 CI run 41399368174 (deterministic; checked by CI VellumCore tests)
entries.note: The same taps: points read from the strokes near the tip (each such stroke's points once, for its ends, corners and centre). Before: every point on the canvas. New with #8.

entries.measured: perf/release-baselines 2026-11-04 GitHub xcode-27 hosted runner, Xcode 27.2, iPhone Duo simulator iOS 27.1, Debug build, the benchmark alone, with the drag layer rasterized; 4 jobs of 3 launches, CI run 41764008766
entries.note: Main-thread busy time per display frame (DebugBenchmark), indicative only, on a shared simulator at 60 Hz. A lasso selection of 657 strokes above the eraser's band at everything, lifted onto its own layer when the Pencil lands (in the set-up), dragged 240 frames, dropped on the last. Each frame moves one transform. Until #32 the slow frames came throughout the 240 frames with about 2 ms of main-thread CPU in about 30 ms of wall time: the main thread waited on the render server, which stroked every path of the moved layer again each frame. The layer is rasterized for a move now, so the render server draws it once. The before is the baseline from one run, with the layer as paths. The value is the upper quartile of those launches (a max, their median), not scaled: the probe does not follow this job's timings.
